stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +53.8%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $297.15 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-29, 11 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-09.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-03) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
stories.excerpt: Ukraine competes with Russia and data centers for China’s optical fiber supply.
stories.lead: Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting.

stories.title: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in Oviedo
stories.excerpt: Officers attended the scene in connection with a separate incident at a residential building in the city.
stories.lead:
A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a shooting.

The blast happened when officers from Spain's canine unit and explosives disposal unit arrived and examined a suspicious backpack following reports of a dispute between neighbours on Tuesday morning.

A woman who had been shot and the injured officer have been taken to hospital for treatment.

stories.title: France threatens actions against Iran over supermarket cyberattacks
stories.excerpt: France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage.
stories.lead:
France's foreign minister said Tuesday that Paris ruled out "nothing" to respond to a major cyberattack on hundreds of supermarket fridges in October that it has blamed on Iran.

Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told FranceinfoTV that Iran's ambassador would be summoned and European-level sanctions would be sought.

"I can also tell you that we rule nothing out and will take all measures – including those we may not disclose publicly – that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks," he added.

stories.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
stories.excerpt: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.
stories.lead:
Late Monday, The Associated Press determined that California voters had rejected Prop 40, the proposed billionaire wealth tax I wrote about last week. Given the big blue wave we saw during the midterms, why did this tax on billionaires fail to surf to victory?

To make sense of the results, I went back to the two economists I spoke with last week: UC Berkeley's Gabriel Zucman, a leading champion of wealth taxes, and Stanford's Joshua Rauh, a prominent critic of Prop 40.

Last week, they disagreed on what this wealth tax on billionaires would do to California's economy and tax revenue. Now comes the sequel, in which they disagree on what the results say about the politics of wealth taxes.

stories.title: Denmark women’s national team returns with Nordic Championships bronze
stories.excerpt: Denmark's rebuilt women's national water polo team won bronze at the Nordic Championships in Stockholm, its first senior international tournament in many years. The post Denmark women’s national team returns with Nordic Championships bronze appeared first on Total Waterpolo .
stories.lead:
Denmark’s women’s national water polo team is back. At the Nordic Championships in Stockholm at the end of September, a squad rebuilt this year finished with bronze, its first senior international tournament in many years.

According to the team, the previous national side folded about five years ago as players moved away and clubs closed. Coaches Tina Ammitzbøll and Mette Eskelund, who both played on that earlier team, took the lead in bringing it back. Vandpolo Danmark, which presents the senior women’s programme, names the same pair as the coaches behind the restart, with Linda Rose as team leader.
